items.summary: The doc says the third rendered part is 'the type arguments', glossing over `argString`'s documented fallback (bracketed component type of the runtime class when it's an array with no explicit type arguments). The sibling `AbstractTypeManifest.toString` doc two hunks later, which calls the exact same `argString` method, spells this fallback out explicitly ('otherwise the bracketed component type of the upper bound if the upper bound is an array class, and otherwise nothing'). The inconsistent level of detail for the same underlying method reads oddly side by side; consider either trimming both to 'argString' or expanding both consistently.

The @return text 'the `arrayManifest` of `arg` cast to `Manifest[T]`' is syntactically ambiguous — it can be misread as '(the arrayManifest of arg), cast to Manifest[T]', which would be wrong since the return type is `Manifest[Array[T]]`. The intended (and correct) parse is 'the arrayManifest of (arg cast to Manifest[T])', matching `arg.asInstanceOf[Manifest[T]].arrayManifest`. The adjacent method signature disambiguates it, but rephrasing (e.g. 'the `arrayManifest` obtained by casting `arg` to `Manifest[T]`') would remove the ambiguity. Appears identically in both the `Manifest` object and `ManifestFactory` copies.
